previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including sclerosing mesenteritis, chronic gastrointestinal dysmotility, osteoporosis, and chronic pain was admitted for acute left-sided rib pain after lifting a bag. A chest X-ray showed no fractures or acute lung issues, and she declined a CT scan due to radiation concerns. She was treated with Toradol and a Lidoderm patch for musculoskeletal pain. During the admission, she requested IV Dilaudid for worsening chronic abdominal pain, but the medical team, in consultation with pain management, determined it was contraindicated due to risks of worsening GI motility. After being informed of this decision, she elected to leave the hospital. She was discharged home with increased Lovenox, her home medications, and follow-up plans with her pain and GI specialists.

GASTROGRAFIN STUDY:
FINDINGS: 
  
After drinking 200 mL of Gastrografin, an abdominal radiograph 
performed 10 minutes later showed contrast within the stomach, 
duodenum and proximal jejunum.  A radiograph obtained at 25 
minutes demonstrated contrast reaching the distal jejunum.  
There is persistent dilation of the duodenum measuring up to 5.6 
cm.  The proximal jejunum is also dilated measuring up to 6.5 cm 
and the distal jejunum is collapsed.  The overall appearance of 
the bowel is unchanged from ___ when it was slightly 
more dilated.  Contrast reached the cecum by 45 minutes. 
  
IMPRESSION: 
  
Unchanged appearance of the small bowel from multiple prior 
exams with no 
evidence of obstruction as the contrast promptly passed to the 
cecum.  Stable appearance of dilated small bowel. 

 
Brief Hospital Course:
# Suicidal ideation: Pt was discharged on day of admission 
(Please see discharge summary for ___ at her request when she 
was not given IV dilaudid.  She told her son she was going to 
kill herself then pulled her femoral line. She was seen by 
Psychiatry who initially placed her on 1:1 sitter, in context of 
___. Patient continued to express SI for several days, 
perseverating on the fact that she needed dilaudid or she would 
kill herself by either using the curtains or jumping out the 
window, or hanging herself in the shower. Psychiatry and Social 
work evaluated the patient. Throughout her admission she 
continued to demand dilaudid while walking through the Unit and 
not appearing to be in any distress. Her SI eventually resolved. 
Of note, she has made suicidal comments during prior admissions 
when she did not get IV dilaudid.

# nutrition: In order to determine necessity of replacing 
femoral line for TPN, calorie counts were done. Patient was seen 
eating and drinking multiple times by the staff, but would 
always tell us that she is unable to do so due to nausea. On 
___, at the request of her outpatient gastroenterologist Dr 
___ underwent ___ upper GI series. This showed 
contrast moving through to her cecum within 45 minutes of 
contrast administration and appeared grossly unchanged from 
previous studies. Patient was adamant about having the Femoral 
Line replaced, as she had no other access. 

Results of calorie Counts for 2 days:
68% of her calorie goal
29% of her protein goal 

Patient felt that ""she cannot live on this"" and insisted she was 
barely taking in a few bites. Nutrition felt that she may able 
to take in more at home and would be ok without the line at 
least for 10 days. However, she demanded the femoral line. She 
was told that Dr ___ felt it is not indicated at this 
time, and patient decided to leave. She was safe for discharge 
given stable vital signs, adequate PO nutrition, bowel 
movements. Her pain appeared to be at baseline, out of 
proportion to objective findings. The current ___ medical 
team, in conjunction with outpatient providers, find no 
indication for IV dilaudid for Ms. ___.  

# Pseudoseizures: Has started to have seizure-like episodes 
while awake, during which she arches her back, closes eyes 
tightly, and moans. Is distractable during these episodes and 
responsive to pain. Followed by Dr. ___ neurology. She 
states that she has a history of seizures and ""these are not 
pseudo-seizures,  I have been evaluted for these,"" while having 
body shakes. 

# Self-injurious behaviors: Reported that she is hitting herself 
unintentionally. Last did this as a child. She stopped injuring 
herself on day two of this re-admission. 

# IV access: After she pulled out her tunnelled femoral line, 
her only access was a PIV. She was not given TPN during this 
admission. She often lost her PIVs, though which she received 
prn antiemetics.  As there was no indication to urgently replace 
the central femoral line, we recommended using the PR or IM 
route for her analgesics and antiemetics, but she insists these 
routes do not work for her.
  

#TRANSITIONAL ISSUES: 
 #PAIN CONTROL - patient has multiple admissions with workup 
that shows no significant change in her organic bowel disease, 
yet she did receive dilaudid on those admissions. Patient 
continues to demand dilaudid to ""get a break"". The writer feels 
that this is not appropriate for her pain relief and that 
patient should not receive doses of dilaudid. It is felt that 
her life stressors often make her come into the hospital, but 
this should not be treated with dilaudid, and inpatient 
psychiatry should be involved instead, if patient is again 
suicidal or otherwise is in distress when dilaudid is denied in 
absence of evidence of exacerbation of organic disease.
